MINUTES
  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION ADJOURNED MEETING
  FEBRUARY 21, 2023

  1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

  An adjourned meeting of the Park and Activities Commission of the City of Rolling Hills
  Estates was called to order at 7:02 p.m. at City of Rolling Hills Estates Council Chambers,
  4045 Palos Verdes Dr. N., Rolling Hills Estates, California, by CHAIR CIAROLLA.

  2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

  CHAIR CIAROLLA led those present in the Pledge of Allegiance.

  3.  ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present:  Pope, Bain, Ciarolla, McCormick, Persichina and
  Retz (joined at 7:11 pm)

  Commissioners Absent:  None

  City Staff Present:  Community Services Supervisor Rosa Pinuelas
  Community Services Coordinator Matt Morrow

  4.  PRESENTATION

  A.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION REORGANIZATION PRESENTATION

  Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas stated that the City Council appointed
  COMMISSIONER BAIN as Chair and COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK as Vice
  Chair of the COMMISSION.

  COMMISSIONER CIAROLLA was recognized for her service as 2022 Chair of the
  Commission and was provided a plaque for her service.

  5.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A.  PARK & ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING DRAFT MINUTES OF JANUARY
  17, 2023

  COMMISSIONER POPE made a motion, seconded by VICE CHAIR
  MCCORMICK to:

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  1
February 21, 2023
   APPROVE THE PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF
  JANUARY 17, 2023.

  There being no objection, CHAIR BAIN so ordered.

  6.  AUDIENCE ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA

  NONE.

  7.  BUSINESS ITEMS

  A.  PROPOSED NAMES FOR FUTURE PARK SITE LOCATED AT THE
  NORTHEAST CORNER OF PALOS VERDES DRIVE NORTH AND PALOS
  VERDES DRIVE EAST

  Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas provided a staff report (as per the agenda
  material). She presented a new recommended name of Teena Clifton Park provided
  by staff for the Commission’s consideration.

  COMMISSIONER POPE asked about the Founding Fathers of the City and stated
  how it would be difficult to just select one name from the Founding Fathers. She
  also made a recommendation to consider Founders Park as a name along with a
  plaque describing the naming of the park.

  Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas stated that the Commission could decide
  to provide a list of names in priority or just submit a list of names, in response to
  COMMISSIONER CIAROLLA.

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA stated that City Council will ultimately decide the
  name of the park and it would be better to submit a list of names to be considered
  as opposed to one name.

  CHAIR BAIN led the Commission in a discussion regarding the suggested list of
  names in priority. COMMISSIONERS had a brief discussion regarding the priority
  name for recommendation to City Council. Based on a consensus the
  COMMISSIONERS decided that RHE Founders Park be listed as the top choice to
  be recommended for City Council to consider.

  Commission discussion ensued. COMMISSIONER CIAROLLA recommended the
  more general names be included in the list before individual names.
  COMMISSIONERS concurred that Gateway Park, Hillview Park, Pepper Tree Park
  and Triangle Park also be included in the recommendation to the City Council in no
  particular order or priority.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  2
February 21, 2023
   COMMISSIONER RETZ requested to include the name Tongva Park in the list of
  other names. After a brief discussion by the COMMISSION, it was decided that this
  park would not be representative of such a distinguished name of Tongva Park. The
  COMMISSION concurred that the name of Tongva Park would be better suited for
  a different project that may better represent the Tongva people.

  CHAIR BAIN reaffirmed with the COMMISSION that they recommend “RHE
  Founders Park” as the top name considered by City Council followed by the names
  of Gateway Park, Hillview Park, Pepper Tree Park and Triangle Park. She also
  restated that if the City Council chose the name of RHE Founders Park the
  Commission recommended a plaque be installed in the park describing the
  historical aspect of that specific name.

  B.  OVERVIEW OF EVENTS AND ACTIVITIES AT ERNIE HOWLETT PARK

  Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas provided a staff report (as per the agenda
  material).

  Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas provided more detail regarding the park
  permits offered at Ernie Howlett Park, in response to COMMISSIONER POPE. She
  also explained the fee structure regarding a park permit at the park, in response to
  CHAIR BAIN.

  Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas stated that many of the 2022 non-city
  special events are returning to Ernie Howlett Park in 2023 and most have already
  submitted a special event application, in response to COMMISSIONER CIAROLLA.

  C.  PARK CAMERAS UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT)

  Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas provided a brief update, stating that the
  park cameras item will be removed from the Commission’s future agenda section
  as it had become part of a study conducted by the City’s IT Department.

  Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas explained that park cameras will be
  researched as part of this study to decide how to properly implement a park camera
  system, in response to CHAIR BAIN.

  D.  SPORTS FIELD POLICY

  Community Services Coordinator Morrow provided a staff report (as per the agenda
  material).

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  3
February 21, 2023
   COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA asked whether a for-profit could apply through the
  school district. Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas stated that staff would ask
  the school district questions to determine if it is a school district program. She also
  stated that the application would need to include a certificate of insurance from the
  school district if it was for one of their programs.

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA asked about the parameters regarding the coach
  to player ratio in the clinic section. Community Services Coordinator Morrow stated
  that typically a coach to player ratio is 10:1 to 15:1 to provide a safe and effective
  program.

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA asked whether the City is or would charge hourly
  fees for the camps. Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas stated that the Group
  B organizations currently pay a flat yearly fee for field use, and staff would have to
  investigate whether to charge an extra hourly fee if a camp was offered outside an
  organization’s standard season period.

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA asked whether the City would require sport
  specific training for the camp instructors in the Group B camp section. Community
  Services Coordinator Morrow stated that staff would review with the City Attorney
  whether the sport specific training stated in another section of the policy would
  encompass the entire policy or if that would need to be mentioned in the other
  sections as a separate line.

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA asked if the suggested price cap of $350 for a full
  week of a full day Group B sports camp was too high and whether that amount
  should be lowered. The COMMISSION discussed the pros and cons of keeping the
  cost as written or presenting a lower cost. After further discussion with responses,
  it was decided that it would be best for staff to provide a sports camp price
  comparison sheet to present to the Commission at the next meeting to determine a
  proper price cap.

  CHAIR BAIN asked to better understand the definition of a City sponsored program.
  Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas and Coordinator Morrow further
  described organizations considered to be City sponsored. After additional
  discussion, COMMISSION directed staff to include a refined definition on what a
  City sponsored organization entails so as to better understand what a City approved
  program represents.

  It was suggested to table the item to the next Parks and Activities Commission
  meeting to allow staff to make suggested modifications to the sports field policy as
  drafted and provide some additional information for the Commission to consider
  before a making a recommendation to City Council.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  4
February 21, 2023
   E.  TENNIS CLUB OPEN HOUSE (VERBAL REPORT)

  Community Services Coordinator Morrow gave a brief overview of the Tennis Club
  Open House which included a description of the activities, time frame, and
  marketing of the event.

  8.  COMMISSION ITEMS

  A.  ADOPT-A-PARK (VERBAL REPORT)

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA provided a list regarding some of the infractions
  and issues regarding the use of Ernie Howlett Park by Silver Spur Little League
  (SSLL). COMMISSIONERS held a brief discussion on the best practices regarding
  how to respond to these ongoing issues with Silver Spur Little League. Staff stated
  that they would be speaking to the President of Silver Spur Little League in depth
  regarding these items, in response to COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA

  Discussion ensued regarding how to ensure compliance of the SSLL issues
  discussed. Staff indicated that there are plans to reinstitute a pre-season meeting
  between staff and the league president and any board members of these
  organizations. Staff also stated that they will add a procedures section to the sports
  field policy regarding any infractions.

  VICE CHAIR MCCORMICK stated that there are some tree limbs down on the trail
  at George F Canyon between mile marker 4 and mile marker 10.

  B.  MATTERS OF INTEREST (VERBAL REPORT)

  VICE CHAIR MCCORMICK inquired about if there are any other sites the City may
  be considering for any additional pocket parks. He mentioned the parcel of land
  between George F Canyon Preserve and Taber Park would be a nice location to
  consider. He also inquired that there are two barn structures on City land around
  that same area and if there was an update regarding the structures. Community
  Services Supervisor Pinuelas responded that she will research these items and
  report back.

  9.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

  A.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS OF JANUARY 24, 2023

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

  B.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS OF FEBRUARY 14, 2023
  RECEIVED AND FILED.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  5
February 21, 2023
   C.  SOUTH BAY COUNCIL OF GOVERNMENTS GENERAL ASSEMBLY – MARCH
  23, 2023, 9AM – 3PM

  Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas provided information regarding the
  assembly and the location.

  10.  FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

  A.  PETER WEBER EQUESTRIAN CENTER RESTROOMS

  NONE.

  B.  CAPITAL IMPROVEMENT PROJECT LIST

  CHAIR BAIN asked about the other interest and fees line in the Pepper Tree
  Foundation financials that were presented during last month’s meeting. Community
  Services Supervisor Pinuelas informed CHAIR BAIN that she would update her
  regarding this topic.

  CHAIR BAIN proposed a future agenda item for the Commission to think of other
  events and activities that may be able to bring extra funds to the Pepper Tree
  Foundation.

  11.  ADJOURNMENT

  CHAIR BAIN MOVED TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS:

  ADJOURNED THE MEETING AT 8:35 PM TO THE NEXT PARK AND ACTIVITIES
  COMMISSION MEETING ON MARCH 20, 2023, AT 7:00 P.M., WHICH WILL BE
  HELD AT THE CITY HALL COUNCIL CHAMBER.

  There being no objection, CHAIR BAIN so ordered.

  Respectfully submitted,  Approved,

  __________________________  ___________________________
  Matt Morrow  Judy Bain
  Community Services Coordinator  Chair, Park & Activities Commission

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  6
February 21, 2023
